subject.title: [Feature]: Cron job output routing — hard-coded destination for job results (file, channel, session)

question: Should OpenClaw add framework-owned cron output targets for file, channel, and session destinations, and what safety/ownership boundary should that API use?
rationale: The requested fix adds public cron config plus scheduler-owned file writes, channel sends, session injection, fallback behavior, and run-status semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the product and security contract.

options.title: Design Output Contract First
options.body: Approve a single `output` contract with explicit file containment, target authorization, partial-failure semantics, protocol/docs updates, and tests before any implementation PR.

options.title: Narrow To Existing Delivery
options.body: Keep this issue open but scope the first implementation to extending existing chat/webhook delivery only, leaving file and session injection for later decisions.

options.title: Reject Core Expansion
options.body: Close or defer the request if maintainers decide cron output routing should remain prompt/tool-owned rather than scheduler-owned.

recommendation.title: Design Output Contract First
recommendation.body: Approve a single `output` contract with explicit file containment, target authorization, partial-failure semantics, protocol/docs updates, and tests before any implementation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron schema/protocol and delivery-validation history makes this the best available routing owner for the product/API decision.
